source: NICE NG245, Asthma: diagnosis, monitoring and chronic asthma management (BTS, NICE, SIGN), 27 November 2024. Recommendations 1.1.2, 1.2.1-1.2.4, and the committee rationale on pages 41-42.
note: Prose is original and hand-written per the repo rule against lifting stems from commercial banks. Stems follow docs/stem-style.md, feedback and resolutions follow docs/explanation-style.md. Screening decisions are in asthma-diagnosis-ng245.md. Draft for review -- not yet in src/cases.json, and no batch assigned.

clauses.feedback: Her age does not affect this decision.

clauses.text: reports eight months of cough and chest tightness, waking her at night and worse after exercise.
clauses.feedback: This history is what puts her in the pathway. NG245 does not confirm asthma without a supporting objective test.

clauses.text: She has hay fever and her mother has asthma.
clauses.feedback: Hay fever and a family history raise the probability, but neither is an objective test and neither confirms the diagnosis.

clauses.text: She has never smoked and takes no medication.
clauses.feedback: Not smoking removes a competing explanation, and taking no inhaled steroid means her results are not suppressed. Neither confirms asthma.

clauses.text: Her eosinophil count is within the laboratory reference range and her FeNO is 32 ppb.
clauses.feedback: Both are rule-in tests with deliberately high cut-offs. A FeNO of 32 does not exclude asthma; it means the pathway continues.

clauses.text: After salbutamol her FEV1 rises from 1.50 to 1.69 litres, against a predicted 2.90.
clauses.feedback: The rise is 12.7% of baseline but 190 ml. NG245 asks adults for 12% and 200 ml, or 10% of predicted.

clauses.text: She is diagnosed with asthma and started on maintenance inhalers.
clauses.feedback: This is the plan you are being asked to judge, not a finding about the patient.

none.feedback: The recorded diagnosis is not supported by the tests in front of you, so the plan cannot stand.

resolution.lead: NG245 confirms asthma on bronchodilator reversibility only if the FEV1 rise is 12% and 200 ml, or 10% of predicted. Hers is neither, so the diagnosis is not confirmed and she is coded as suspected asthma.

points.text: Eosinophils and FeNO — within range, and 32 ppb against a 50 ppb cut-off
12% and 200 ml — the rise is 12.7%, but it is 190 ml
10% of predicted — 190 ml against a predicted 2.90 litres is 6.6%

resolution.trap: Starting an inhaled steroid before the diagnosis is confirmed also closes the door on confirming it: FeNO and spirometry are more likely to be normal once treatment has begun, so the tests she still needs are the ones she has just had made harder to read.
